entries.core_move: Map each real-valued time instant $t$ to its signal value $x(t)$, using the function viewpoint to interpret continuous-time signal notation before graphs, piecewise definitions, support, symmetry, and basic parameters.
Determine $x(t_0)$ from a continuous-time signal graph by locating the specified time on the horizontal axis and reading the corresponding vertical value.
Convert graphical or functional continuous-time signal descriptions into piecewise definitions by assigning each time interval its correct expression and boundary condition.
Identify the support and zero regions of a continuous-time signal from a graph, formula, or piecewise definition by marking the intervals where $x(t)$ is nonzero versus identically zero.
Classify a continuous-time signal from its graph or piecewise definition as even, odd, or neither by comparing $x(t)$ with $x(-t)$ over matching positive and negative time regions.

entries.lesson_title: Basic Signal Parameters: Amplitude, Offset, and Duration
entries.core_move: Extract amplitude, vertical offset, and duration from graphical or piecewise continuous-time signal descriptions by identifying extrema, baseline level, and nonzero support interval.
